data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001's argument is undermined by its own counterconditions. It claims the expert is more reliable because the checklist is 'lossy compression' that cannot account for dynamic interdependencies, but it concedes that under extreme stress or sleep deprivation the expert's intuitive synthesis degrades. This concedes that expert intuition is not intrinsically more reliable—it is conditional on the expert's state. Since the problem asks which will 'on average' produce more reliable judgments, a method (checklist) that does not degrade under stress plausibly has higher average reliability across the realistic distribution of conditions, undercutting SRC_001's blanket claim that the single expert 'remains more reliable.' The target never reconciles this tension or establishes that high-interdependence tasks dominate the average.
